topup.title: Top up
topup.checkoutFailed: The checkout could not load; try again or pick another rail.
topup.finishPayment: Finish the payment in the form above — the wallet credits when the switch's webhook lands. Nothing is charged until you confirm.
topup.hyperswitchNote: Mounts the switch's Unified Checkout in place; the deposit confirms through the Hyperswitch webhook once the payment succeeds. A deployment without the rail configured hides it.
topup.receiptReplays: This request already landed; the receipt replays.
topup.keepContentHash: Keep contentHash — it names the ledger entry a bill verifies against.
topup.manualIntro: Record a payment that arrived out of band; the credit lands immediately. For card payment use Stripe; for an operator-minted code use the redemption rail.
topup.manualConsequence: This books {{amount}} onto your balance immediately.
topup.stripeIntro: Opens the hosted Stripe checkout; the deposit confirms through the Stripe webhook once the session completes. A deployment without Stripe configured answers 503.
topup.stripeConsequence: This opens Stripe's hosted checkout; you aren't charged until you confirm there.
topup.noStripeRail: This deployment has no Stripe rail configured.
topup.airwallexIntro: Opens the hosted Airwallex payment page; the deposit confirms through the Airwallex webhook once the intent succeeds. A deployment without Airwallex configured answers 503.
topup.airwallexConsequence: This opens Airwallex's hosted payment page; you aren't charged until you confirm there.
topup.noAirwallexRail: This deployment has no Airwallex rail configured.
topup.hyperswitchIntro: Mounts the switch's Unified Checkout in place; the deposit confirms through the Hyperswitch webhook once the payment succeeds. A deployment without the rail configured answers 503.
topup.hyperswitchConsequence: This creates a payment intent and mounts the switch's checkout below — nothing is charged until you complete it.
topup.noHyperswitchRail: This deployment has no Hyperswitch rail configured.
topup.redeemIntro: An oxr-… code the operator minted. Unknown, spent, or expired codes all answer 404 — which of the three it is stays the holder's business.
topup.redeemConsequence: This claims the code's value onto your balance immediately; a spent code can't be reused.
topup.paymentConfirmed: Payment confirmed — {{amount}} landed on the balance.
topup.paymentTimeout: No credit landed within a minute. If you completed the payment the webhook is still on its way — the balance catches up on its own; if you cancelled, nothing was charged.
topup.paymentWaiting: Waiting for the payment to confirm… the switch's webhook credits the wallet; this updates as soon as it lands.

settings.title: Settings
settings.verificationSent: Verification email sent; check your inbox.
settings.displayNote: The ledger always keeps credits — this is only how the dashboard and the statement PDF render them. Set a code and a rate per credit (e.g. USD at 0.0014 ≈ $1.40 per 1,000 credits); leave the code empty to render credits alone. The conversion is presentational — a bill's proof covers the credits, never the fiat figure.
settings.rendersAs: This organization renders credits as ≈ {{rate}} {{code}} per credit, {{decimals}} decimals.
settings.ownerOnly: (only an owner or an admin may change it)
settings.twoFactorNote: A confirmed authenticator gates every password login behind a live six-digit code — or a single-use backup code — so a stolen password alone cannot open the session.
settings.twoFactorOn: Two-factor authentication is on. Save these backup codes — they are shown this once, each works a single time.
settings.addSecretNote: Add this secret to your authenticator — scan the link or type the base32 — then prove it with a live code.
settings.liveCodeHint: the six digits the authenticator now shows
settings.turnOffHint: a live code disables the confirmed factor
settings.deleteNote: This cannot be undone. Your password confirms the deletion.
settings.deleteExplain: Deleting the account is irreversible: the email is tombstoned, sessions and API keys are revoked, memberships end — except that an organization's last owner is refused. Bills keep verifying; the ledger never carries identity. OAuth-created accounts need a real password (set one through the reset flow) to confirm this.

channels.name: Name
channels.driftNote: Price drift is probed from each channel's GET /api/v1/pricing catalog — an oxsum-compatible endpoint. A channel pointing at a real provider serves no such catalog, so its cost signal is the upstream bill sync, not this probe.

deposits.empty: No deposits yet — a top-up, a code redemption or a rail payment appears here.
deposits.statusNote: Statuses are the rails' facts: pending (opened, not paid), confirmed (the rail says paid, the ledger has not credited yet), credited (the entry named on the row moved the wallet), reversed (a refund or chargeback — the Entry cell then names the reversal's own entry) or expired. A received amount appears only when the rail reported a different figure than the deposit was opened for. Reversing posts one ledger entry taking the purchased credit back — and for a rail that moves money back (the Hyperswitch switch) it issues the rail's refund too: the row then shows `refund pending`/`succeeded`/`failed` under the status, `failed` meaning the rail refused the call so a retry re-issues it. `disputed` marks a charge the rail reported contested.
deposits.reverseHint: required, it becomes the reversal entry's description

margin.empty: No settled turns yet — a row appears once a gateway turn settles and its upstream cost is recorded.
margin.note: The provider bill is what the upstream billed the channel, summed per day by the upstream-bill-sync pass; “not reconciled” means that pass has not billed the channel yet, not that it billed nothing. The total counts each channel once — the API repeats the channel-scoped figure on every model row. Untracked turns are settled turns with no upstream cost recorded (an untracked price, a swept hold, or history), so a growing gap there is where missing upstream pricing shows up first.

metering.credentialHint: a service credential minted under 'credentials' — bearer on /api/v1/metering/*
metering.holdKeyHint: the key a holds answer returned
metering.oneShotNote: An event that already ran — declared usage bills at the code's latest mode: event price, hold and settle in one answer.

organizations.displayCurrencyHint: ISO code + rate per credit, e.g. USD / 0.0014
organizations.suspendSpendHint: new holds refuse; in-flight still settles
organizations.creditNotesNote: A reasoned credit for this organization: it posts a new ledger entry (Revenue debited, Wallet credited) and moves no money. It is not a refund.
organizations.reasonRequiredHint: required — it becomes the entry's description
organizations.noCreditNotes: No credit notes issued to this organization yet.
